description: Self-written report about curl's dynamic buffer: one real function, one correctly quoted line, and one line the reporter got wrong. Covers symbol CONFIRMED and file/line CONFIRMED + CONTRADICTED.

report.title: Heap overflow in dynbuf append
report.body:
I think there is a heap overflow in curl 8.23.0.

The function `curlx_dyn_add` in lib/curlx/dynbuf.c appends a string to a dynamic buffer by calling `dyn_nappend`, which copies the data at line 115:

    memcpy(&s->bufr[idx], mem, len);

There is no size check before it: line 82 is the same `memcpy(&s->bufr[idx], mem, len);` with nothing in front of it, so a long string overflows the buffer.

claim.statement: curlx_dyn_add is a function in lib/curlx/dynbuf.c
lib/curlx/dynbuf.c line 115 is memcpy(&s->bufr[idx], mem, len);
claim.source_excerpt:
which copies the data at line 115:

    memcpy(&s->bufr[idx], mem, len);

claim.statement: lib/curlx/dynbuf.c line 82 is memcpy(&s->bufr[idx], mem, len);
claim.source_excerpt: line 82 is the same `memcpy(&s->bufr[idx], mem, len);`

evidence.note: Line 82 is the size check that rejects an append that would not fit; the copy is at line 115.
